A_target.statement:
Let $Y$ be a non-negative [[Definition:Random Variable|random variable]] and $t > 0$.
Then:
:$\map \Pr {Y \ge t} \le \dfrac {\expect Y} t$

B_source.statement:
Let $U, V$ be [[Definition:Random Variable|random variables]] with $0 \le U \le V$.
Then:
:$\expect U \le \expect V$

substitutions.the smaller variable U: t times the indicator t*1_{Y >= t}

validity_conditions: The pointwise inequality t*1_{Y>=t} <= Y holds because Y >= 0 everywhere and Y >= t exactly on the indicator's support.
Monotonicity of expectation applied to U = t*1_{Y>=t} and V = Y gives t*P(Y>=t) <= E[Y].
proof_plan:
By [[Expectation is Monotone|monotonicity of expectation]]:
:$t \map \Pr {Y \ge t} = \expect {t \cdot \chi_{\set {Y \ge t} } } \le \expect Y$

Dividing by $t > 0$:
:$\map \Pr {Y \ge t} \le \dfrac {\expect Y} t$
which is [[Markov's Inequality]].
{{qed}}
